newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli police undecided on corruption probe.
newsitem.headline: Israeli police undecided on corruption probe.

text.p: Israeli police said on Friday they had yet to decide whether to investigate charges of corruption in the appointment of an attorney general by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government.

Police spokeswoman Linda Menuhin told Reuters she had incorrectly stated earlier an investigation would be launched on Sunday. "Sunday morning...they will decide whether to open an investigation," she said."

Israel's state-owned television alleged attorney general Roni Bar-On, who resigned his post after serving for 12 hours two weeks ago, had promised a plea bargain to a member of the Shas coalition party standing trial on corruption charges.
In return, Shas would support an Israel-PLO deal on the West Bank town of Hebron, the television said.
Everyone named in the report has denied the allegations.

"The police haven't decided yet whether to open an investigation," Menuhin said. "First of all head of investigations Sando Mazor will meet acting Attorney General Edna Arbel...They will decide whether to open an investigation or not."
